F5_rule: cp2 ruling F5 (planning chat, 2026-10-17): every registered CO2 reference scheme is carried; a pass must hold under the lowest-onset scheme and counts only with a solvated sink; a falsification must hold under every registered scheme; a solid-salt falsification stands, a solid-salt pass is inconclusive; otherwise inconclusive.
aggregation_over_salts: electrolyte_salts lists three options and none is registered as the electrolyte. verdict_by_salt gives each option; verdict_any_registered_salt is the worst over them (rule 2 of theory Eq. th:eq:sink if every option's anion is admissible) and verdict_all_registered_salts the best (the phase is falsified as a design only if every option falsifies it).

extensions.scope: Thermodynamic proxies only: a stability domain, a decomposition energy or a window says which state is at equilibrium, never how fast anything corrodes, dissolves or decomposes.

limitations: The electrolyte's own anodic stability limit (oxidation of the anion or the solvent) is not assessed: above it the electrolyte reacts first, and it may lie below any limit here (theory section 9).
Measured anodic onsets of Al in fluorine-free electrolytes (key al_onset_ffree) are a comparator, not an input.
Reduction limits use 0 K energies; solid entropies are neglected in every scheme, the gases carry their absolute entropies (gas_reference.md quantifies that approximation).
The Ca2+ and Al3+ solvation free energies relative to Li+ (keys solvation_ca_vs_li, solvation_al_vs_li) are gaps, so no solvated-sink limit exists and no pass can count.
